retained.comment: Tip from the numbers side: if your Canva Pro is for your business, it's a business expense. Keep the invoice, and if you also use it personally, only the business share counts.

retained.what: Spooky things that haunt small business owners
retained.comment: The scariest one for new sole traders: the first tax bill. Nothing gets withheld from ABN income, so it all lands at once. Moving a slice of every payment into a separate account the day it arrives takes the fright out of it.
Spookier still: a shoebox of receipts in June. You generally need to keep business records for 5 years, so snapping receipts as you go saves the scramble.
Handy for cash flow. If you account for GST on a cash basis, the GST follows the instalments as they're actually paid, too.
Nothing beats a local bakery that knows your order before you say it. Fitzroy's lucky.

returnpolicy.comment: Good trick. And if any of those subscriptions are genuinely for work (software, professional memberships), the work-related share may be claimable at tax time. Keep the receipts.
Buying a laptop or monitor in the sales mostly for work? Keep the receipt. Work items costing $300 or less can be claimed straight away (the work-use share). Over $300 gets claimed over a few years.
Another one people miss: salary sacrificing into super. It's generally taxed at 15% going in, which can be less than your income tax rate. Worth checking the caps first.

returnpolicy.what: Irish Linen House with a separate residence
returnpolicy.comment: That independent two-bedroom part is interesting tax-wise. Rent it out and its expenses can be claimed against the rent, but it can also reduce the main-residence CGT exemption for that portion when you sell.
The biggest money leak for most people isn't coffee. It's not keeping receipts and missing deductions at tax time.
